utterances.text: Well, I'm going to deal with part of it, and then if you can later --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no. If you start your sketch on this format, we have to finish.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: Can the map be moved up and then we will see the area that I'm trying to show. If the entire map can be scrolled up. Or if not, could it be zoomed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could the map please be scrolled up a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, when did you take up -- or rather, what was the area of defence that you took up?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: Well, do you want me to draw that down the borderline?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can see that clearly on the map. We would like to see the actual points, from where to where, and also locations in the interior.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: I'd like to draw it along the borderline.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. That would be the borderline. Roughly, that would be the direction of my zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What is the length of the front line, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: Along the line of the border, that's about 150 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, what happened there? What -- what was put on the map? Oh, sorry, I'm looking at one which is on the other side of the screen. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Do I have to repeat any question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, that's okay. I can see it clearly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, you said 150 kilometres, that that was the length of the front line.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the length down the borderline, along the front line, as we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about in depth?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: Up to 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps this is my last question for today, because our time seems to be up. Could you please tell me, for a motorised brigade like your brigade was, how big should that area be?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC
utterances.text: According to the principles involved, it should be a manoeuvring ground, 12 to 15 kilometres; in mountainous and hilly ground, 15 to 20 kilometres; and in mountainous ground like this one, it can be even up to 25 kilometres, in terms of the front line. And in depth, it can also be 20 to 25 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, is -- is this map one that was originally drawn by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is my work map. One can see that this is the 9th of April, 1999. I originally ordered it to be drawn, but I'm not the one who actually does the drawing. It's my operations man, my operations officer who does that, an officer who was specially trained to draw maps, but according to the elements that I give him, according to the elements that I directly give him on the map. He directly puts that on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you arrange for Mr. Cepic and his team to get this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I know that I had this map in 2005 when I was a witness at the trial of the late President Milosevic. Perhaps this map dates back to that time and has been here since then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And was it you that arranged to get the map for your previous appearance as a witness here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2005? In 2005, the then-legal advisors of President Milosevic provided a large number of maps. I remember that. Among others, I think there were 15, 20 of them. One of them is this map. I'm not sure, but perhaps this map was submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor as far back as in 2002 through the investigator in Belgrade, who asked for my work maps. And I think that all of those that were there then in the archives were handed over to him. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you know the source of this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We took this map in the JDB electronic system. If you are asking specifically about our Defence team, we took it from the Milosevic files, and that's why it's so good in e-court. Unfortunately, our equipment is not that good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, do you know the source of this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you can find out any more on that subject for tomorrow, then I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- make my best efforts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to interrupt your evidence there -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. Can we please have an IC number assigned to this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC 149, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Delic, we have to interrupt there for the day and resume tomorrow. That will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. I don't think in this courtroom. I think -- Court III. So you need to be back ready to resume at that time. Meanwhile, as you know from your previous attendance here, it's vital that you should have no communication with anyone at all, no matter who, about the evidence in this case, and that means any part of the evidence. Put what's going on to the back of your mind. Talk to people about other things and come back here refreshed, ready to resume at 9.00 tomorrow. Now could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
